props.title: All the President's Men
props.initialSlug: Two reporters expose Watergate, topple Nixon

sections.content: All the President's Men revolutionized political thrillers by showing real journalism's methodical grind. Director Alan J. Pakula crafts unbearable tension from phone calls, typewriters, and whispered conversations in parking garages. Robert Redford and Dustin Hoffman's electric performances as Bob Woodward and Carl Bernstein capture the obsessive drive of reporters chasing a story that would bring down a presidency. The film's influence echoes through modern journalism dramas like Spotlight (2015) and The Post (2017), but none match its documentary-like attention to the unglamorous details of newspaper work.

sections.content: The 1970s marked a golden age for paranoid political thrillers reflecting post-Watergate distrust in institutions. Three Days of the Condor (1975) and The Parallax View (1974) imagined vast conspiracies, while Network (1976) predicted media's descent into sensationalism. These films shared All the President's Men's shadowy visual style - what cinematographer Gordon Willis called "the democracy of darkness" - where truth hides in dimly lit corners and fluorescent-lit offices mask sinister secrets.

Modern whistleblower films like The Insider (1999) and Dark Waters (2019) follow All the President's Men's template: determined professionals sacrificing everything to expose corruption. But Pakula's film stands apart by showing journalism as detective work - each revelation earned through meticulous fact-checking and source cultivation. The film's famous "follow the money" line inspired generations of investigative reporters. SUBHEAD: Impact on Modern Political Cinema

sections.content: The film's influence extends beyond journalism movies. Its visual language - deep shadows, telephoto surveillance shots, labyrinthine institutional spaces - became shorthand for institutional corruption in films like Zodiac (2007) and The Report (2019). Even superhero movies like Captain America: The Winter Soldier (2014) borrow its conspiracy thriller DNA. But what sets All the President's Men apart is its faith that truth, methodically pursued, can still triumph over power.
